note: Feature Toggle: feature definitions (name/label/description) live in config feature_toggle.features (features.<name>); on/off status lives in the key-value store (collection feature_toggle, key flags = [name => bool]), NOT config or state. Services: feature_toggle.feature_manager (FeatureManagerInterface - CRUD of Feature value objects) and feature_toggle.feature_status (FeatureStatusInterface - getStatus/setStatus, dispatches feature_toggle.update event, clears cache tags feature_toggle_list / feature_toggle:<name>). configure route feature_toggle.feature_toggle_form (/admin/config/system/feature_toggle). Drush feature_toggle:set NAME 0|1 (alias ftset). Twig feature_toggle_status(). Consumers: Condition plugin feature_toggle, Views access plugins feature_toggle_feature/perm_feature/role_feature, route requirement _feature_toggle, drupalSettings.feature_toggle.enabled. Permissions: administer feature_toggle, modify feature_toggle status. Medium/hard cases create namespaced features (ft_*) via the manager service and read/write their config definition and key-value status.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site using the feature_toggle module, what Drush command turns a feature on or off from the command line, and what arguments does it take?
evals.expected_output: drush feature_toggle:set <name> <value> (alias drush ftset), where <name> is the feature machine name and <value> is 1 (on) or 0 (off), e.g. drush feature_toggle:set beta_checkout 1.

evals.prompt: How do I check whether a feature_toggle feature is enabled from inside a Twig template?
evals.expected_output: Use the Twig function feature_toggle_status('feature_name'), which returns a boolean, e.g. {% if feature_toggle_status('beta_checkout') %}...{% endif %}.

evals.prompt: In the feature_toggle module, where are feature definitions stored versus where is each feature's on/off status stored?
evals.expected_output: Feature definitions (name/label/description) are stored in the config object feature_toggle.features under features.<name>. The on/off status is stored separately in the key-value store (collection feature_toggle, key 'flags' = [name => bool]) - so toggling a feature is not a config change.

evals.prompt: This site has a feature_toggle feature with the machine name ft_known. Inspect the running site and state whether ft_known is currently enabled or disabled.
evals.expected_output: ft_known is enabled (on). Its status flag is true in the key-value store (collection feature_toggle, key flags), i.e. FeatureStatusInterface::getStatus('ft_known') returns TRUE.

evals.prompt: This site defines two feature_toggle features, ft_on and ft_off. Inspect the running site and state which of the two is currently enabled.
evals.expected_output: ft_on is enabled and ft_off is disabled (per the key-value 'flags' map / FeatureStatusInterface::getStatus).

evals.prompt: Using the feature_toggle module on this site, define a new feature with the machine name ft_task (give it a human-readable label). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add the feature via the feature manager, e.g. \Drupal::service('feature_toggle.feature_manager')->addFeature(new Drupal\feature_toggle\Feature('ft_task', 'Task Feature')); (or the UI at /admin/config/system/feature_toggle/add). Afterwards FeatureManagerInterface::featureExists('ft_task') is TRUE (config feature_toggle.features.features.ft_task exists).

evals.prompt: This site has a feature_toggle feature ft_switch that is currently turned off. Turn it on and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable it, e.g. drush feature_toggle:set ft_switch 1 (or FeatureStatusInterface::setStatus($feature, TRUE)). Afterwards FeatureStatusInterface::getStatus('ft_switch') returns TRUE (the key-value flag is true).
